task: Discover the supported Moss/FileIO surface before designing the filesystem SDK
observation: The required bootstrap result exposed language_version moss-0.1, the phase20_fileio_executor capability, fixed-size read/write requirements, Range borrowing, and the explicit Fast Debug limitation. That discovery let the implementation use a bounded 4096-byte wrapper and avoid inventing dynamic reads or an interpreted FileIO backend.
impact: Reduced design uncertainty and made the package contract match the compiler/runtime instead of a guessed host API.

resolution.summary: Implemented the supported bounded native wrappers and documented the unsupported surface.

suggestion: Keep FileIO capability and static-bound facts in the bootstrap source surface.

task: Probe a reusable FileIO helper with a caller-supplied request size
observation: A helper calling file.read(offset, size) was rejected with FILEIO_UNBOUNDED_REQUEST even though size was an Int parameter. The documented rule requires a statically provable finite request bound; a fixed literal 4096 call compiled and executed.
impact: The fs API must expose bounded operations or repeated fixed-size calls rather than a conventional arbitrary-size read helper.

resolution.summary: This is the Phase 20 safety contract, not a missing runtime primitive; moss.fs documents the fixed bound and exposes read_prefix.

suggestion: If variable-size reads are added later, expose an explicit bounded-request type or compile-time bound mechanism.

task: Run native package tests for a package whose exported functions use FileIO
observation: margo test linked the package test harness without the FileIO host symbols (moss_solo_enter, moss_solo_leave, and file registry functions). A real root consumer built through Margo linked and ran correctly, so acceptance moved to an external native consumer script under tests/check_native.py.
impact: The SDK cannot rely on the ordinary package-test harness for FileIO execution; native/release evidence requires an application consumer. This is documented rather than hidden as a passing package test.

resolution.summary: Use generated native and source-free consumers for FileIO acceptance; Fast Debug is explicitly checked as unsupported.

suggestion: Provide the production FileIO host shim when linking package test executables, or document the external-consumer acceptance pattern as the supported test path.

task: Implement pure lexical path manipulation without host dependencies
observation: String.chars, Vector[String], bounded loops, and inferred local types were sufficient to express POSIX normalize/join/basename/dirname/extension/stem and component-boundary checks without compiler changes or runtime access.
impact: The pure moss.path package remains independently importable and its behavior is easy to test against POSIX reference cases.

resolution.summary: Pure path APIs and differential tests pass on the current language surface.

task: Add a total-allocation-bounded regular-file reader without changing FileIO request rules
observation: A fixed 4096-byte FileIO request can be combined with a caller limit: the implementation checks the borrowed Range length before copying it, returns an owned Vector[Int] up to the limit, and raises a tag-only FsError when the next chunk would overflow. Unique repository-local temporary fixture directories also let native, release, and source-free consumers run without colliding with other tests.
impact: moss.fs now offers a bounded read contract while preserving static request bounds, borrowed Range lifetime, typed errors, and isolated test execution.

resolution.summary: read_limited and unique temporary fixture coverage passed native debug/release and compiled-only ABI-v9 checks.

tool_used: Margo native builds and ABI-v9 consumer checks
